summary: Tested new Settings > Download Audio feature end-to-end. Backend: 10/10 pytest tests pass covering list filtering (no signed_off, no soft-deleted audio), consent gate (400 without consent), signed_off policy (400 on the leftover-audio_file_id case using meeting 4b948235), admin list returns 22 rows, manager list is filtered to only their own sign_off meetings, direct-endpoint 403 when a manager tries a meeting reassigned to another sign_off_manager, audit_logs row written with user_name + 'IP:' in detail for 2 consecutive downloads, and attendee cannot list. Frontend: Settings tab 'Download Audio' renders between Branding and Focus Topics, lists 22 meetings for admin, search filter works ('Jane Smith' → 2 rows), Data Protection Notice modal opens with org name 'Test Company' correctly interpolated (dynamic, not literal), confirm button correctly disabled until checkbox ticked, real blob download triggered with filename 'Supervision_with_Demo_User.wav'. All main acceptance criteria pass including the two the main agent had not yet exercised (manager-vs-manager 403 direct-endpoint call and signed_off rejection).
critical_code_review_comments: DownloadAudioTab.js hardcodes filename extension as '.wav' (line 104) but the underlying storage is audio/webm — the file will download as e.g. 'Supervision_with_Demo_User.wav' while its actual container is webm. Consider using the Content-Type header (or storing/returning original_filename which the backend already reads from audio_files) to pick the correct extension, or at minimum use '.webm'/audio blob type match. Low severity — file opens fine in most players, but the extension is misleading and could confuse forensic/legal handoff which is the actual use case for this feature.

meetings.py download_audio() derives client IP from X-Forwarded-For's LAST element (line ~878: `xff.split(',')[-1]`). In the standard XFF convention the FIRST element is the original client and the last is the closest proxy — so on multi-hop deployments the audit log will record the ingress/CF IP rather than the user's IP. Given this is a compliance/audit feature explicitly meant to capture 'who' downloaded, worth using the first element (or a trusted-proxy-aware lib) so audit_logs.detail reflects the real user's public IP.

GET /downloadable-audio has no pagination / hard cap. Large orgs with thousands of unsigned meetings + audio will get a very large payload and slow render (list currently uses max-h-96 scroll but fetches everything). Consider ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT (default 100) + search-side query param to filter on server.
